work_or_witness: ‘ʻŌlelo Resource of the Month: The importance of moʻolelo’ · title and paras. 50–53
literal_gloss: story, narrative, history; no single English gloss fixed here
definition: The University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo publication calls its Hilo account moʻolelo and closes with a phrase it says is used at the end of moʻolelo.
cultural_caution: Do not reduce moʻolelo to ‘myth’, ‘legend’, lore, or a game quest. This pass preserves it as a source-native framing term in one contemporary institutional publication.

supports: The publication frames the account as moʻolelo and discusses honoring place names, people, and lessons carried by moʻolelo.

work_or_witness: Maui Field Trip · p. 20, ‘Māui Catching the Sun’
definition: In the selected Māui-and-Lā account, Lā is the named sun and is given speech and negotiates with Māui.
cultural_caution: The character-level representation is limited to personification in one cited account. It must not be promoted to a universal Hawaiian solar-deity category or a cross-setting monster/boss analogy.

supports: The selected account names Lā as the sun and gives Lā speech and agency.

work_or_witness: ‘ʻŌlelo Resource of the Month: The importance of moʻolelo’ · para. 27
definition: The selected Hilo publication glosses the charge given to Hinaikeahi and Hinaikawai as kuleana to take care of people in their respective places.
cultural_caution: This local narrative relation should not be generalized into a game duty system, property title, moral alignment, or universal Polynesian law.

supports: The publication says Hina gives each daughter an area and charges each with the kuleana of taking care of its people.

work_or_witness: ‘ʻŌlelo Resource of the Month: The importance of moʻolelo’ · paras. 29–30 and 39–45
definition: The selected Hilo account identifies the imu as an underground oven pit used for cooking and makes it central to the Hinaikeahi and Hinaikawai episodes.
cultural_caution: An imu is not a fantasy altar, trap, fire-spell focus, or resurrection device. Its narrative use in this one account does not define all uses of an imu.

supports: The publication defines the imu and narrates its role in the two sisters’ actions.

work_or_witness: ‘ʻŌlelo Resource of the Month: The importance of moʻolelo’ · para. 39
literal_gloss: a context-dependent sacred/divine term; no single gloss fixed here
definition: In the selected Hilo account, Hinaikeahi speaks of offering herself to the akua; the publication adds that akua is a general term referring to gods and that there were many akua in ancient Hawaiʻi.
cultural_caution: The publication’s English ‘gods’ gloss is not a warrant to classify akua as a generic pantheon, species, or D&D-style deity type. No generic akua become character nodes in this pass.

supports: The selected publication uses akua in the Hinaikeahi account and supplies its limited English explanation.
